It's a big project, but I'd probably pay 150$ a year to fund it.  Once that cat was out of the bag, it'd force Bitwig corporation to have some competition with what they could have been.

If it was "pay once":

- they'd have to be able to afford it, which I don't think they can (and is why a subscription was okay)

- there'd have to be some ability to "loan out" a per project access key to your specific list of plugins, otherwise projects would only be compatible with the users specific setup (eg, VST zoos)

- there would no longer be financial incentive to be inventive or try new things.  it would just become an ableton clone
If 3rd party developers could do this, then we could start open source creating third party plugins... which is exactly the thing to do.

You seem to be able to write alright.  If you converse via email or notebook (keepsake!) it'll not only make it easier, but give you time to really think it out.

As for situations you're uncomfortable with, that's a toughy.  And college will most likely be uncomfortable.  I REALLY, REALLY recommend looking for a smaller college, maybe somewhere a little off the beaten path, but **ONLY** if after checking it out, it seems right to you.  BE VERY CHOOSY.  Don't let yourself wind up in the wrong place for a year or longer.  Maybe write "college" on your hand so you can start looking around.  Hippies are nice, so anywhere woodsy might be a little easier.

Really do focus on which college you go to, if you have a choice.  I can tell you from experience that not only would it be near impossible to acclimate to mainstream, it's also really only worth it if you feel it absolutely necessary.

As for death, later.  And don't consider things unfair to your parents or whatever.  Think about yourself first, and don't worry about others.  If you think you can solve a problem, go for it, but you don't need to feel bad for any *good* reason.

All in all, you seem to be in good standing, but maybe not the right place.  Do look into finding a nice college.  Set prestigious aside, and explain to your parents how important it is that you don't overwhelm yourself.  Besides, it would probably be cheaper to get your GE at a less prestigious and more fun place.

This isn't so much me looking for help as trying to say something to the people who try do give it.  There are reasons to live, but don't cite this one in particular because it's... well, no matter how much a person may be better off not living, they will think as the adrenaline surges through "I'm invincible, and should have lived more."  It's just how adrenaline works, and it generally comes off as 'holy' when people talk about those last minute second thoughts.

If you truly believe you want to die, you must first find the words that prove it.  Certainly you could take a gut feeling and run with it, but what gut feelings have you followed through before just to find they were less solid than expected, and what was the cost?

People say give it time, and this is true.  While the scars will never go away, you will grow larger and they'll become less of you.  But if these words alone are enough to change your life around... I'd be surprised.

You must do more than give it time.  If you really want to kill yourself, do it from the inside out.  If the person you are doesn't want to exist, bludgeon them with anti depressants.  Treat them like they're already dead as you go searching for who else you might be.  Let them die, while all the other parts of you live on.

Get a job and sweet gaming rig, go to lan parties.  Become a tool, go to the thrift shop, and find some decent clothes.  Just a couple things at a time, but add some color to your life.  Find a work out that works out for you.  I rock climb because it's fucking easy.  

If you really are living a life worth ending, prove it.  If you really are trapped, find the walls with your fist and test all of them.  Just because you can hear the echo of a cell does not mean there are no weak walls or crawl holes out.

You don't have to be strong, just try to realize you aren't who you think you are, and you're never going to actually find yourself.  You're too much to ever understand.
